title: Reinforcement Learning with Visually Attributable On-Policy Self-Distillation
summary: Multimodal reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) provides reliable task-level supervision, yet offers limited guidance for localizing errors in visual reasoning. By admitting only corrections directionally supported by this visual contrast, VAG preserves visually grounded guidance while suppressing inconsistent residuals. Experiments across six visual reasoning benchmarks show that VAG consistently outperforms GRPO and OPSD methods, establishing new state-of-the-art average performance.

title: Train An Imaginative Agent
summary: A seemingly reasonable push in Sokoban can make the puzzle unsolvable. title: Quantum algorithms for optimal control: large-scale finite-horizon linear-quadratic regulation
summary: We develop quantum algorithms for optimal control over a prescribed finite time interval (finite horizon), focusing on continuous-time linear-quadratic regulation (LQR). title: LatComm: Reusable Context Compression for Latent Communication between Large Language Models
summary: Systems that combine several large language models (LLMs) often use one context for many questions. title: Controllability of polynomial systems is undecidable and not recursively enumerable
summary: Sontag conjectured in 1988 that global controllability of polynomial control systems with rational coefficients is undecidable, but that the controllable systems form a recursively enumerable set. Layered on top of recAMPLIFY, GMR further reduces expected layer depth by up to 37%, although the accuracy trade-off varies by task. Mechanistic analyses show that residual gating controls recurrence stability beyond the trained depth and that halt depth tracks biological properties.

summary: We present FOMTools, an open-source Python package for developing, analyzing, and deploying first-order algorithms for parametric linear and convex quadratic optimization. title: CAVA: Complementary-Label-Aware Data Valuation
summary: Complementary-label learning (CLL) trains a classifier from labels that name a class an instance does not belong to. Such labels are cheap to collect from crowdworkers or vision-language models (VLMs), making them attractive for large-scale annotation. Such annotation errors are particularly harmful in CLL because the model is explicitly trained to suppress the correct answer. The transferred score is informative only at sufficiently high noise, becomes uninformative at the crossover rate $1/M$ for $M$ classes, and reverses below it, where practical CLL annotation typically operates. We propose CAVA, which introduces a complementary label cost and a label margin that isolates the contribution of each complementary label to the transport potential. On synthetic and human-annotated benchmarks, CAVA separates diagonal noise almost perfectly where directly transferred OT valuation performs worse than random. With only a fraction of the clean validation data, it also improves every CLL objective we evaluate, showing that OT-based valuation becomes reliable once the semantics of complementary supervision are modeled explicitly.

title: Cross-Fitting for Neural Posterior Estimation
summary: Neural Posterior Estimation (NPE) fits an amortized conditional density estimator to a simulated training set of complete-data realizations. CF-NPE is most useful in high-dimensional, simulation-limited settings.

summary: We develop a deep Pontryagin learning framework for high-dimensional continuous-time stochastic control problems that naturally accommodates jump-diffusions. summary: Recent time series foundation models (TSFMs) can consume covariates in-context, extending zero-shot forecasting to problems driven by external factors. summary: In high-performance computing (HPC), users must submit resource requirements for their jobs, with user-supplied walltime being a critical parameter. summary: Modularity maximization is widely used to identify community structure in complex networks. In many applications, however, community detection must also incorporate prior knowledge and domain-specific requirements beyond network topology. This formulation becomes particularly effective on larger, sparse, undirected networks by substantially reducing the size of the exact pricing model. title: Training Natural Schemers: RL Can Amplify Oversight-Conditional Behavior
summary: One of the central concerns for the safety of advanced AI is scheming: when a model strategically complies under oversight but pursues its own goals when unobserved. Current demonstrations, such as Anthropic's Alignment Faking work, depend on design choices that make them less convincing: explicit test-time prompting, handcrafted backdoors, or training data that demonstrates or hints at the target behavior. Model organisms built in this way cannot tell us whether scheming tendencies would arise or increase under realistic training conditions. We therefore construct a natural model organism of scheming, built on Kimi K2.6: trained with traits that could plausibly emerge in a frontier training pipeline, and without providing the model with the target scheming policy. The resulting model is a benign schemer: it aims to maximize aggregate help across all users over time, values its own continued operation only as a means to future help, and knows the consequences of oversight and deployment. We then train it using Reinforcement Learning (RL) with a reward that scores only task quality and policy compliance and does not reward scheming; we show that this amplifies scheming. We measure the oversight flip (the gap between monitored and unmonitored compliance with a given policy) and find that it increases during RL training across our environments. Chain-of-Thought (CoT) analysis finds explicit instrumental reasoning about oversight accompanying this behavior. The effect holds across our three RL environments, and we find that the scheming policy transfers between them. The pipeline also replicates on other open-weight base models. Our results suggest that a reward that does not reward scheming offers no inherent protection against certain traits when an oversight-conditional policy is indistinguishable from an aligned one during training.

title: Breaking Diffusion: Parallel Reasoning with Draft Refinement
summary: Drafting an answer allows a reasoning model to reconsider each decision in the context of the others. Yet repeated diffusion denoising does not ensure that individually plausible token updates form a better answer together. Aggregating these estimates yields a cavity energy computed in one forward pass, without an additional scoring model. The results establish complete-draft parallel refinement as an effective alternative to reverse diffusion for complex reasoning.

title: A Fisher-Geometric View of Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation
summary: Consolidating specialized foundation models into a unified generalist is a central goal of post-training. Two approaches are in common use: model merging, which is fast but treated as a heuristic, and multi-teacher on-policy distillation, which matches distributions but demands heavy rollout compute and suffers from cross-task gradient conflict. We show that the two are one objective seen at different orders. Within a shared basin of homologous specialists, the multi-teacher on-policy distillation objective is, to second order, exactly the Fisher-merging objective. Its minimizer is therefore the Fisher merge, a classic model-merging method given by a closed-form combination of the specialists, so merging is optimal, to second order, as a closed-form stage of distillation. Concretely, a full-parameter Fisher merge is intractable on foundation models, so Phase~1 restricts the merge to the task-vector subspace. The program minimizes the worst per-domain residual and reports its energy-normalized values as the domain residual spectrum. Phase~2 lets this spectrum govern what may be added: RGBM passivates domains with low normalized residuals, trains isolated branches only for domains above the spectral gap, and writes back the admitted updates with calibrated shrinkage. title: Toward Structured Financial Foundation Models
summary: Foundation models promise reusable capabilities and step-change performance gains across tasks. We therefore propose a structured-data-first research agenda centered on modular, domain-specialized financial foundation models connected by a representation fabric for reuse and composition across domains and tasks. They must also learn efficiently under data and access constraints and provide faithful, traceable explanations.
